direction: amodal completion, 3D reconstruction and 3D amodal completion
method: ARIS research-lit style problem-gap analysis followed by idea-creator style hypotheses; no GPU experiments launched

papers.title: S2C-3D: Sparse-to-Complete: From Sparse Image Captures to Complete 3D Scenes

paper_fact: Uses pi3 for sparse-view camera and point-cloud initialization.
Finetunes a scene-specific diffusion model on degraded and input images.
Plans virtual cameras with information gain and uses view-consistency conditioned sampling.
evidence_explanation: The three components address domain gap, insufficient coverage and cross-view conflicts as a causal loop.
The ablation table supports the necessity of mask finetuning, trajectory planning and consistency conditioning.
research_hypothesis: Separating observed, inferred and uncertain Gaussian evidence can improve hidden-geometry calibration.
UAV view selection should optimize uncertainty reduction rather than only geometric coverage.
Object-centric temporal memory can prevent moving objects from corrupting static-scene Gaussian optimization.

papers.problem_gap: Sparse-view reconstruction leaves unseen regions, domain mismatch and cross-view conflicts; post-hoc hole filling does not enforce one global explanation.
papers.why_method_needed: The failure is a closed-loop acquisition and consistency problem, not only an image quality problem.
papers.why_may_work: Scene adaptation supplies target-specific priors, information gain adds new evidence, and reprojection energy constrains repaired views to a shared geometry.
assumptions_and_failures: Requires usable coarse cameras and depth from pi3.
Static-scene and input-frustum assumptions exclude many dynamic/open scenes.
Concave rooms, random cameras inside objects and greedy planning can produce wrong geometry.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: Table 1 reports best PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS across ScanNet++, Replica and S2C-Scene; Table 2 shows degradation when each of the three key components is removed.
papers.unresolved_gaps: No explicit observed/inferred/unknown labels, calibrated uncertainty, dynamic-object memory or multi-hypothesis output.

ideas.name: Evidence-Decomposed S2C
ideas.method: Predict observed, inferred and uncertain evidence types for each Gaussian and use visibility-aware losses.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Evidence separation reduces high-confidence hallucination in hidden regions.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Occlusion-stratified hidden-region CD, PSNR and calibration error on Replica/ScanNet++.
ideas.risk: Extra branches may only add capacity.
ideas.relation: Extends S2C-3D scene adaptation and consistency loop.

ideas.name: Uncertainty-Guided UAV Active Completion
ideas.method: Generate multiple completions, estimate uncertainty reduction for candidate views and choose a safe UAV waypoint.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Uncertainty reduction is a better next-view objective than coverage alone.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Compare random, coverage-greedy and uncertainty-guided trajectories in synthetic outdoor scenes.
ideas.expected_contribution: A bridge between 3D amodal completion and active perception.
ideas.risk: Uncertainty may measure sampling noise rather than true error.
ideas.relation: Replaces S2C-3D information gain with uncertainty gain.

ideas.name: Dynamic Object Tokens
ideas.method: Maintain static background Gaussians and object-centric temporal tokens with reprojection-based memory reset.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Separating moving objects prevents temporal fusion artifacts.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Three-to-five-frame sparse inputs; measure 3D jitter, hidden-region CD and identity drift.
ideas.risk: Tracking errors can route wrong evidence into object memory.

papers.title: Amodal3R: Amodal 3D Reconstruction from Occluded 2D Images

paper_fact: Uses a conditional 3D generative model for occluded 2D observations.
Introduces mask-weighted multi-head cross-attention and occlusion-aware attention.
Trains on synthetic data and evaluates real occluded scenes.
evidence_explanation: Direct 3D generation avoids cascading 2D inpainting boundary errors.
Occlusion attention can inject shape priors but may bias unusual objects toward common templates.
research_hypothesis: Explicit occluder geometry and depth order will improve hidden-surface recovery.
Category-agnostic structural tokens can reduce long-tail template bias.

papers.problem_gap: Visible-surface reconstruction and 2D-completion-then-3D pipelines do not directly model hidden 3D structure.
papers.why_method_needed: The target is a complete object, so the model must reason beyond visible pixels in 3D.
papers.why_may_work: Object-level latent features combine visible evidence with learned shape priors and occlusion weighting.
assumptions_and_failures: Depends on reliable object crops and masks.
Synthetic-to-real shift and nonstandard topology can cause plausible but wrong completions.
Scene-level clutter and unknown categories remain unproven.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: The abstract states synthetic-only training, occlusion-aware attention and gains over 2D completion followed by 3D reconstruction.
papers.unresolved_gaps: Open-world scene completion, multi-view fusion, temporal consistency and uncertainty calibration.

ideas.name: Occluder-aware latent
ideas.method: Condition on visible mask, occluder mask and depth order.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Explicit occluder geometry improves hidden-surface inference.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Compare hidden-surface CD by occlusion ratio.
ideas.risk: Depth order may be unavailable in real data.

ideas.name: Category-agnostic structural tokens
ideas.method: Disentangle category semantics from reusable geometric structure tokens.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Structure tokens generalize better to held-out categories.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Train on seen categories and test on held-out categories.
ideas.risk: Disentanglement may discard useful category priors.
ideas.relation: Keeps Amodal3R's latent but changes factorization.

ideas.name: Multi-view amodal fusion
ideas.method: Generate per-view hypotheses and fuse them with cross-view consistency.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Additional unposed views reduce ambiguity without requiring dense pose labels.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Compare one, two and four views.
ideas.risk: View association errors create conflicting shapes.

papers.title: GENA3D: Generative Amodal 3D Modeling by Bridging 2D Priors and 3D Coherence

paper_fact: Bridges learned 2D generative priors and explicit 3D reasoning.
Uses View-Wise Cross-Attention and Stereo-Conditioned Cross-Attention.
Reports synthetic and real-world amodal evaluations.
evidence_explanation: 2D priors improve plausible appearance while stereo-conditioned attention anchors geometry.
Cross-view alignment is necessary to prevent independently attractive but incompatible views.
research_hypothesis: Evidence-ranked sampling can improve geometric validity without retraining the generator.
Scene relation constraints can reject physically impossible completions.

papers.problem_gap: 2D priors lack reliable 3D coherence; pure 3D generation may lack expressive appearance priors.
papers.why_method_needed: Amodal completion needs both plausible hidden appearance and a single coherent 3D explanation.
papers.why_may_work: View-wise attention aligns observations and stereo conditioning injects spatial relationships.
assumptions_and_failures: Requires meaningful view relationships and reliable matching.
A strong 2D prior can hallucinate attractive but input-inconsistent details.
Sampling cost and calibration are not established by the abstract alone.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: The abstract explicitly claims improved synthetic and real-world amodal modeling; detailed numerical verification is deferred because the PDF was not downloaded for browse reading.
papers.unresolved_gaps: Uncertainty calibration, open-world categories, dynamic objects and scene-level physical relations.

ideas.name: Evidence-ranked sampling
ideas.method: Rank generated candidates by visible reprojection, depth order and local geometry.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Evidence ranking improves correctness without changing the generator.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Random versus evidence-ranked selection under increasing occlusion.
ideas.risk: Ranking may favor conservative incomplete shapes.

ideas.name: Diffusion uncertainty calibration
ideas.method: Map sample variance to hidden-surface error and calibrate confidence.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Diversity is informative when conditioned on visible evidence.
ideas.risk: Variance may reflect aleatoric and model noise together.

ideas.name: Scene-graph constrained generation
ideas.method: Filter samples violating support, contact or occlusion relations.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Physical relations remove plausible-looking but impossible geometry.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Physical violation rate before and after constraints.
ideas.risk: Relation labels and estimators can be noisy.
ideas.relation: Adds scene context absent from object-only modeling.

papers.title: TACO: Taming Diffusion for in-the-wild Video Amodal Completion

paper_fact: Targets video amodal completion in unstructured real-world videos.
Uses a conditional video diffusion model and progressive fine-tuning.
Builds synthetic occlusion videos and tests downstream reconstruction and pose estimation.
evidence_explanation: Temporal diffusion manifolds provide repeated evidence but can also propagate an early mistake.
Progressive difficulty reduces training instability under severe occlusion.
research_hypothesis: Joint 2D-3D temporal consistency is safer than 2D temporal consistency alone.
Memory reset based on visible reprojection can limit error accumulation.

papers.problem_gap: Frame-wise amodal completion flickers and fails on in-the-wild occlusions.
papers.why_method_needed: Video provides repeated observations that can constrain hidden content and identity.
papers.why_may_work: Video diffusion captures temporal structure; curriculum-like fine-tuning exposes increasing occlusion difficulty.
assumptions_and_failures: Requires usable correspondence and motion estimation.
Long complete occlusion supplies no new evidence.
Camera shake, fast motion and object reappearance can break temporal assumptions.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: The abstract supports broad real-video evaluation and downstream reconstruction/pose applications; no unverified numeric claims are recorded here.
papers.unresolved_gaps: 3D correctness, long-occlusion uncertainty, dynamic non-rigid objects and domain-specific UAV data.

ideas.name: Bidirectional 2D-3D consistency
ideas.method: Jointly constrain mask tracks and 3D shape tracks.
ideas.core_hypothesis: 3D reprojection catches temporally stable but geometrically wrong 2D completion.

ideas.name: Occlusion-event segmentation
ideas.method: Use separate handling for short, long and reappearing occlusions.
ideas.core_hypothesis: One temporal loss cannot cover all visibility transitions.
ideas.relation: Makes TACO's curriculum explicit at inference.

ideas.name: Memory reset detector
ideas.method: Reset temporal memory when visible reprojection error rises.
ideas.core_hypothesis: A visible-region diagnostic can detect stale hidden predictions.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Inject tracking failures and measure recovery.
ideas.risk: Frequent resets may remove temporal benefits.

papers.title: Occlusion-Aware Temporally Consistent Amodal Completion for 3D Human-Object Interaction Reconstruction

paper_fact: Targets dynamic human-object interaction reconstruction from monocular video.
Uses amodal completion and temporal context under mutual occlusion.
Validates with 3D Gaussian Splatting on challenging videos.
evidence_explanation: Object-centric temporal reasoning is needed because human and object motion violate static-scene assumptions.
Temporal coherence stabilizes recovery but can propagate tracking errors.
research_hypothesis: Visibility-state transitions should be modeled explicitly.
Contact and support relations can improve dynamic amodal geometry.

papers.problem_gap: Static or fully visible 3D reconstruction breaks for mutual occlusion in dynamic interactions.
papers.why_method_needed: The hidden structure and identity of human/object parts must remain coherent across frames.
papers.why_may_work: Temporal context supplies repeated evidence, while amodal completion fills currently hidden structure.
assumptions_and_failures: Needs stable tracking and depth ordering.
Fast motion, camera shake and reappearance can corrupt incremental refinement.
Template-free prediction may struggle with unusual geometry.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: The abstract states improved occlusion handling and temporal stability with 3DGS; detailed metrics remain unverified in browse mode.
papers.unresolved_gaps: Open-world object categories, cross-camera transfer, uncertainty and UAV-scale scenes.

ideas.name: Object-centric temporal memory
ideas.method: Separate static background Gaussians from instance-level temporal tokens.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Measure 3D jitter and identity drift under synthetic occlusion.
ideas.risk: Tracking errors can route wrong evidence.

ideas.name: Visibility-state transition model
ideas.method: Predict visible, occluded and reappeared states and use state-specific losses.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Different visibility transitions require different update rules.

ideas.name: Contact-aware completion
ideas.method: Add hand-object contact and support constraints to the hidden geometry.
ideas.relation: Adds scene relation evidence to the interaction setting.

papers.title: DeOcc-1-to-3: 3D De-Occlusion from a Single Image via Self-Supervised Multi-View Diffusion

paper_fact: Generates six structurally consistent novel views from one occluded image.
Uses occluded/unoccluded pairs and pseudo-ground-truth views for self-supervised training.
evidence_explanation: Multiple generated views turn a single partial observation into several geometric constraints.
Structural consistency is necessary so the views describe one object rather than independent hallucinations.
research_hypothesis: Selecting a reliable subset of generated views can improve 3D reconstruction.
Keeping multiple view sets is more honest than collapsing to one completion under severe occlusion.

papers.problem_gap: Single-image 3D reconstruction assumes full visibility and degrades when the object is occluded.
papers.why_method_needed: The missing views can be synthesized to provide complementary constraints without manual hidden-surface labels.
papers.why_may_work: Self-supervised occlusion pairs teach structure-aware completion and multi-view diffusion supplies consistent observations.
assumptions_and_failures: Synthetic occlusion must resemble real occlusion.
Generated view consistency may still hide a shared wrong prior.
Long-tail, asymmetric and non-rigid objects remain difficult.
papers.author_claims_and_evidence: The abstract supports six-view generation, end-to-end fine-tuning and a new benchmark; no numeric result is asserted here.
papers.unresolved_gaps: Uncertainty calibration, open-world multi-object scenes and cross-view depth verification.

ideas.name: Geometry-ranked view set
ideas.method: Rank generated views by depth and reprojection consistency before 3D reconstruction.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Discarding inconsistent synthetic views improves geometry.

ideas.name: Multi-hypothesis 1-to-3
ideas.method: Generate multiple six-view sets and retain a calibrated candidate set.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Hidden geometry is multi-solution and should not be averaged.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Best-of-N CD, coverage and calibration by occlusion level.
ideas.relation: Extends the paper's generative multi-view idea.

ideas.name: Open-world relation conditioning
ideas.method: Condition view generation on support, contact and occlusion relations in cluttered scenes.
ideas.core_hypothesis: Scene relations constrain object completion better than appearance alone.
ideas.minimum_experiment: Physical relation violation rate in multi-object scenes.
ideas.risk: Relation detection errors can misguide generation.
ideas.relation: Moves from isolated objects to open scenes.
